meta.index.title: VirtuO – virtual orienteering courses for iPhone, Apple Watch and Android
meta.index.description: Run real orienteering courses even after the controls have been collected. Download the course from Livelox, start it in VirtuO, and your phone or watch tells you when you reach a control. Works on iPhone, Apple Watch and Android.

index.on-android-virtuo-sends-a: On Android, VirtuO sends a notification to your phone at every control, so any smartwatch that shows phone notifications will buzz. No separate watch app is needed. It works the same way on iPhone: any smartwatch that receives iPhone notifications will buzz – an Apple Watch is not required. On Apple Watch, VirtuO also runs as its own watch app: once the course is sent to the watch, you can run without your phone.
index.iphone-and-apple-watch-are: iPhone and Apple Watch are trademarks of Apple Inc.; Android and Google Play are trademarks of Google LLC. Livelox, OCAD and Purple Pen are trademarks or brand names of their respective owners. IOF XML is a data format of the International Orienteering Federation (IOF). VirtuO is an independent app and not a product of these companies. Livelox logo used with permission.
index.no-account-no-server-courses:
• No account, no server. Courses and runs are stored only on your phone and watch.
  • Location: GPS is used only during a run, to detect controls. Your location is never sent anywhere.
  • Apple Health (Apple Watch only): only the watch app writes to it, and only if you turn on workout recording in the settings. The iPhone app does not write to it. We read nothing else. There is no such link on Android.
  • Livelox: when you sign in, we only download public course data. We never see your password.
  • No ads and no tracking.
privacy.effective-date-2026-11-19: Effective date: 2026-11-19 · VirtuO (iPhone, Apple Watch, Android)
privacy.in-short-no-account-no: In short: no account, no ads, no tracking, and we sell no data. Your courses and runs stay on your own device.
privacy.the-developer-of-the-app: The developer of the app, Tamás Csikós (Hungary). Contact: support@virtuo.run.
privacy.what-the-app-stores-and: What the app stores, and where
privacy.only-the-apple-watch-app: Only the Apple Watch app can write to Apple Health, and only if you switch on "Save to Health" in the settings (it is off by default). The workout, route and heart rate are then saved. The iPhone app does not write to Health. There is no such link on Android.
privacy.signing-in-to-livelox-is: Signing in to Livelox is optional. You sign in on Livelox's own page (OAuth), and VirtuO never sees your password. The sign-in token is kept in the device keychain (iPhone) or secure storage (Android Keystore). Only public course data is downloaded. Livelox has its own privacy policy.
privacy.virtuo-run-uses-no-cookies: virtuo.run uses no cookies, analytics, ads or tracking code, and loads no external fonts or scripts. If you pick a language in the language menu, your browser remembers it locally (localStorage); this never reaches us. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages; like any web server, GitHub keeps technical logs (for example IP addresses) for security and operation. See the GitHub Privacy Statement.
privacy.because-the-data-is-on: Because the data is on your device, you control it: deleting the app removes all local data. You can end the Livelox sign-in by signing out.
privacy.if-this-policy-changes-we: If this policy changes, we update it here together with the effective date. Questions? Write to support@virtuo.run. See also: Support.
privacy.courses-and-runs-loaded-courses:
• Courses and runs: loaded courses, runs and split times are stored only on your phone and watch. The app has no server of its own and does not ask for an account.
  • Files you open: IOF XML and GPX files are processed on your device and are not uploaded anywhere.
  • No ads, no analytics, no tracking, and we do not sell data to anyone.
privacy.the-app-uses-gps-only:
• The app uses GPS only while a run is active, to detect when you reach a control. This also works with the screen locked and the phone in your pocket, which is why it asks for background location permission.
  • VirtuO does not send your location anywhere; after a run it keeps only the split times, not your route. Exception: if you turn on saving to Apple Health in the Apple Watch app, the route is saved there (see below).
  • The Livelox event search may use your approximate location once to suggest your country. Your phone's operating system (Apple, or Android/Google) converts it to a country code, which may involve that provider's own service; VirtuO does not send it to a server of its own, because there is none. If you do not grant permission, the phone's region setting is used instead.

support.the-iphone-apple-watch-version: The iPhone / Apple Watch version is coming soon to the App Store and the Android version to Google Play. Until then it is in closed testing; you receive the invitation by e-mail.
support.how-do-i-sign-in: How do I sign in to Livelox?
support.in-the-app-open-the: In the app open the Livelox import and choose sign in. Livelox's own page opens and you sign in there; VirtuO never sees your password. Then you can search for an event and pick your class.
support.how-do-i-export-iof: How do I export IOF XML 3.0 from OCAD or Purple Pen?
support.purple-pen-use-the-xml: Purple Pen: use the XML export of the courses and choose IOF XML 3.0. OCAD: choose IOF XML 3.0 in the course export. Menu names may differ between versions. Then open the file with VirtuO (Share / Open with).
support.how-do-i-import-a: How do I import a GPX file?
support.open-the-gpx-file-with:
Open the .gpx file with VirtuO (Share / Open with), or use the file import in the app. The file stays on your device.
Important: the GPX must contain separate points (waypoints or route points). The first point becomes the start, the last one the finish, and each point’s name becomes its control code. A recorded track from a run cannot be used as a course, because it has no separate points.
support.does-it-work-in-my: Does it work in my pocket or with the screen locked?
support.yes-if-you-set-location: Yes, if you set location permission to "Always" (iPhone) or "Allow all the time" (Android). Then the app detects controls even with the screen locked.
support.how-does-the-apple-watch: How does the Apple Watch app work?
support.send-the-course-to-the: Send the course to the watch from the iPhone app; afterwards you can run without your phone. Saving the workout to Health is off by default and can be switched on in the settings. On other smartwatches, notifications tell you about each control.
support.continuous-gps-uses-battery-char: Continuous GPS uses battery. Charge your phone before a long run and enable low power mode if needed; you do not need to keep the screen on, as the app works with it locked.
index.the-next-control-and-the: The next control and the time are visible on the lock screen too
